text:
Predicates:
GoodGuy(x) ::: x is a good guy.
BadGuy(x) ::: x is a bad guy.
SuperheroMovie(x) ::: x is a superhero movie.
NamedAfter(x, y) ::: x is named after y.
InMovie(x, y) ::: x is in movie y.
Wins(x, y) ::: x wins fight y.
Fights(x, y) ::: x fights y.

Premises:
∀x (SuperheroMovie(x) → ∀y (GoodGuy(y) → Wins(y, x))) ::: In superhero movies, the good guys always win.
SuperheroMovie(surprisingAdventures) ::: The Surprising Adventures of Sir Digby Chicken Caesar is a superhero movie.
∀x ∀y (Fights(x, y) → (GoodGuy(x) ↔ BadGuy(y))) ::: Good guys fight bad guys and vice versa.
Fights(sirDigby, nemesis) ::: Sir Digby fights his nemesis.
∀x ∀y ((SuperheroMovie(x) ∧ NamedAfter(x, y)) → GoodGuy(y)) ::: If a superhero movie is named after a character, that character is a good guy.
NamedAfter(surprisingAdventures, sirDigby) ::: The Surprising Adventures of Sir Digby Chicken Caesar is named after Sir Digby.
∀x ∀y (Wins(x, y) → ¬Wins(y, x)) ::: If somebody wins a fight, the person they are fighting does not win.
∀x ∀y ((SuperheroMovie(x) ∧ NamedAfter(x, y)) → InMovie(y, x)) ::: If a superhero movie is named after a character, that character is in the movie.

Conclusion:
¬Wins(nemesis, surprisingAdventures) ::: Sir Digby's nemesis does not win.
